neighbours.label: the opening of a possessive relative clause: ' whose', or ', the X of which' (firing on 'the' … 'of')
fire: The council ordered a survey, the findings of which were never published.
He left a diary, the pages of which had been torn out.
They met a farmer whose barn had burned down in the spring.
It is a small island whose people still speak the old language.
She sang a ballad, the words of which nobody could remember.
The firm hired an engineer whose designs had won several prizes.
We crossed a valley, the floor of which was covered in mist.
He admired a poet whose work he had read as a boy.
quiet: The council ordered a survey, but the findings were never published.
He left a diary, and some pages had been torn out.
They met a farmer who had lost a barn in the spring.
It is a small island where people still speak the old language.
She sang a ballad that nobody could remember.
The firm hired an engineer who had won several prizes.
We crossed a valley which was covered in mist.
He admired a poet he had read as a boy.

notes: Probes: 'whose origin' 0.61, 'whose owner' 0.45, ', the contents of which' 0.65, ', the results of which' 0.23, ', the cost of which' 0.19; plain 'which' 0.11, coordinate 'and the teacher' 0.01. An absolute ', its banks lined' scored 0.39 and ', and its walls' 0.26, so a possessive opening a new noun phrase after a comma may be the wider pattern; the test stays with the relative forms. The opposite pole fires on possessive markers ('s, Korean 의, Chinese 的), so the two poles look like two sides of marking possession.
